$comment: Term list for scripts/audit-whitelabel.mjs.
Copy this file to `.whitelabel-terms.json`, which is git-ignored, and fill in
the terms that must never appear in this repository.
WHY THE LIST IS NOT IN THE REPOSITORY: an audit that enumerates the names it
is looking for becomes the most reliable place to find those names. The check
would then be the single largest trace of exactly what it exists to keep out.
Keeping the list local removes that, and the audit still runs.
The audit FAILS LOUDLY if `.whitelabel-terms.json` is missing, rather than
quietly passing with nothing to search for — a check that cannot fail is worse
than no check, because it is trusted.
Fields per entry:
term  — the string to search for, case-insensitively
word  — true to require a word boundary. Without it, a two-letter
abbreviation matches inside ordinary words and the noise hides the
real hits.
raw   — a regular expression source string, when a plain term is not enough
`allowed` enumerates justified exceptions as `<file>:<term>`, each with a
reason. Some terms legitimately appear as PROHIBITIONS — naming a process the
project deliberately does not have, so nobody reintroduces it. Removing the
term from the search instead would be weaker: the audit would no longer catch
it appearing as real content.

allowed.agent/ux-writing.md:Mustermann: A do-not rule about demo data. The cliché has to be named to be prohibited.
allowed.agent/ux-writing.md:example.com: Recommends the RFC 2606 reserved domains for addresses that must not resolve.
